item.title: Novel Forms and Models of Organization
item.content:encoded:
Masatoshi Kato, Kwansei Gakuin University

David Audretsch, Indiana University

Roy Thurik, Erasmus University Rotterdam

Maksim Belitski, University of Reading

Alex Coad, Waseda Business School

Eric Liguori, Florida State University

Rapid technological change and global interconnection are transforming how firms organize and compete. The special issue examines novel organizational forms that enable companies to achieve exceptional performance, whether through rapid growth without sacrificing efficiency, enhanced resilience to market shocks, or sustained innovation. These forms appear across diverse firm types—from tech giants to micro-enterprises, social ventures, and nonprofits—and across different regional and economic contexts.

The collection seeks research that explores how organizational structures, governance models, and collaboration architectures enable firms to operate at or near the innovation and productivity frontier. Particular interest lies in understanding exceptional performers such as hidden champions, niche leaders, scaleups, and blitzscalers, and how their organizational choices differ across regions, industries, and institutional contexts. The editors welcome comparative analysis spanning developed and developing economies, including underrepresented regions beyond North America and Western Europe.

Appel publié par Journal of Small Business Management. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Organizational forms and firm performance
  • Leadership and decision architecture
  • Make-buy-ally and collaboration strategies
  • Digitalization, AI, and process organization
  • Ecosystem embedment and global value chain orchestration
  • Government relationships and institutional context
  • Business model innovation
  • Hidden champions and niche leaders
  • Scaling and exceptional firm performance
  • Innovation and productivity at the frontier
